s1.syndrome_frame: Bleeding disorder with splenic mass and thrombocytopenia
salient_findings: Bleeding from the mouth, nose, and skin
key_facts: 67-year-old woman
One-month history of bleeding
Splenic mass detected two weeks prior to presentation
No prior medical history
Spleen not palpable on examination
Severe thrombocytopenia with platelet count of 1 × 10^9/L
Thrombocytopenia did not respond to treatment
Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT scan showed splenomegaly with a patchy low-density lesion
Lesion exhibited moderate peripheral enhancement and central hypoenhancement in arterial phase

shortlist.label: Splenic hamartoma
shortlist.why_kept: Preliminary diagnosis made based on imaging findings

shortlist.label: Angiosarcoma of the spleen
shortlist.why_kept: Severe thrombocytopenia and splenic mass with characteristic imaging features

shortlist.label: Littoral cell angioma
shortlist.why_kept: Splenic mass with patchy low-density lesion on CT scan

shortlist.label: Primary splenic lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Splenic mass and thrombocytopenia with potential for lymphomatous involvement

raw.rationale: The patient's severe thrombocytopenia, splenic mass, and lack of response to treatment for thrombocytopenia, along with the imaging characteristics of the lesion, are more consistent with a malignant process such as angiosarcoma of the spleen.

rejected.label: Splenic hamartoma
rejected.why: Hamartomas are typically benign and may not explain the severe thrombocytopenia or the aggressive clinical presentation.

rejected.label: Littoral cell angioma
rejected.why: Littoral cell angiomas are rare, vascular tumors of the spleen, but they are usually asymptomatic and not associated with severe thrombocytopenia.

rejected.label: Splenomegaly with myelofibrosis
rejected.why: Myelofibrosis would likely have other systemic manifestations and bone marrow involvement, which are not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Primary splenic lymphoma
rejected.why: While lymphoma could explain the splenic mass and thrombocytopenia, the imaging characteristics and lack of other lymphadenopathy or systemic symptoms make it less likely than angiosarcoma.
